title: Something in the Water
ending: The machine still existed only in pencil when, the following morning, the newspaper called Daniel Orkleson the man who had cleaned Lake Erie.

blocks.text: Before leaving the shore, Daniel dipped a glass jar into a murky inlet. A blue glimmer slipped beneath the reeds. Behind it, a clear trail widened through the green water. Daniel emptied his cloudy sample and filled the jar again. This time he could see straight through it.

blocks.alt: Daniel examines a clear lake-water sample under his laboratory lamp beside an analog meter and notebook.
blocks.text: Back at the laboratory, he held the jar beneath his lamp. He poured a little into a second jar and stirred in dirt. It stayed cloudy. Whatever had cleared the inlet was still out in the lake.
The boy had come out of that lake able to lift a tree. Now something was clearing the water. Daniel circled both observations in his notebook.

He drew an intake beside a storage unit and began listing parts. Halfway down the page, he checked his accounts. He could build the frame. The instruments and collection equipment were another matter.

blocks.alt: Daniel speaks into a black rotary telephone beside a clear sample jar and a drawing of his proposed lake apparatus; the caller is unseen.
blocks.text: Daniel dialed a number from memory. When someone answered, he shut the laboratory door. “I need funding for a new experiment. At the lake.”
“There’s a blue trail clearing the inlet,” Daniel said. “And a boy who can lift a tree since the flash. I need to find out what’s in that water.”
The voice asked what he needed. Daniel read from his list. “Send it over,” the caller said. “The funding can be arranged.”
Daniel looked at the intake drawing. Money would not keep people from noticing him. “If I start running experiments by the lake, people will ask questions. After what happened with my earlier work—”
The caller ended the conversation. Daniel kept the receiver at his ear for a moment, then put it down and returned to the drawing. He circled the storage unit.
